title: Apprentice Mode — guided onramp sketch
content:
Goal: rapid, low-friction developer onramp for new teams using Redwood inference where cost and complexity are abstracted behind a lightweight guided mode. Not a full product plan — exploratory sketch for prototyping a toggleable 'Apprentice Mode' in the SDK + Console.

Problem statements / why: 
- New teams often request a single quick path: low-cost, low-latency, predictable output with minimal config.
- Current surface includes many knobs (batching, quantization, routing, session cache) which is overwhelming during first week of experimentation.
- Early misconfigurations lead to runaway token spend or perceived instability -> poor retention.

Hypothesis: Provide a curated default profile (Apprentice Mode) that:
- Surfaces a single opt-in toggle in Console and SDK (sdk.apprentice = true)
- Applies safe defaults: conservative max_tokens, aggressive prefix caching, inference fallback to distilled model variants, response trimming heuristics
- Offers a guided checklist in Console (sample prompts, recommended prompt length, visible cost estimator) -> reduces first-week spend and time-to-success

Core user stories (MVP):
- As a small-product engineer, I can enable Apprentice Mode so my team can prototype without worrying about cost spikes.
- As an engineering manager, I can see Apprentice Mode usage and per-route estimated savings in Console.
- As a platform engineer, I can configure tenant-wide Apprentice defaults for internal teams.

Behavioral defaults candidate list (MVP):
- Model selection: prefer small/quantized variant (e.g., redwood-mini-v1) with auto-fallback to larger only on explicit high-quality route.
- Max tokens per request: 128 by default; session-level cap 2k/day per API key (configurable).
- Prefix/KV cache: prewarm with common system prompts; enable session-level sticky snippets to reduce repeated context tokens.
- Response shaping: compress verbosity (truncate to concise mode unless "verbose" hint supplied).
- Telemetry sampling: higher sampling for Apprentice sessions to feed quick UX feedback loop.
- Rate limiting: soft quotas with informative error message linking to upgrade paths.

Console & SDK UX ideas: 
- Console: "Try Apprentice Mode" banner when first creating route; single toggle with summary of tradeoffs and estimated token savings.
- SDK: flag like RedwoodClient(apprentice=True) or client.with_apprentice(). Returns headers: X-Redwood-Profile: apprentice-v1
- Quickstart sample prompts and a cost estimator slider (tokens vs fidelity) in the route creation flow.

Success metrics (first 8 weeks):
- Mean time from sign-up to first successful generation <= 30 minutes for teams who enable Apprentice Mode.
- Average per-team token spend in week 1 reduced by 40% vs control group (no Apprentice).
- Retention (teams with Apprentice enabled) 15% higher at 30 days.
- Net promoter feedback in onboarding flow positive (qualitative).

Experiment plan: 
1) Internal dogfood: opt a few internal projects -> collect telemetry and developer feedback.
2) A/B test on new signups: show toggle vs no toggle. Track cost, time-to-first-call, conversion to paid.
3) Iterate on model choice and compression heuristics based on observed error/regression signals.

Rollout & controls: 
- Config lives in Console as route profile and in SDK as a named profile; profiles have versioning (apprentice-v1, apprentice-v2).
- Allow overrides: teams can pin specific model or disable compression for critical routes.
- Safety: automatic quality monitoring tied to evals; if automated checks detect >5% regressions on held prompt set, revert to previous profile and alert owners.

Risks & open questions: 
- Quality regressions may frustrate users who expect fidelity parity with default offering. Need clear docs and easy toggle to disable.
- Billing complexity: daily caps and soft quotas need clear upgrade messaging to avoid surprise outages.
- Platform complexity: supporting many profiles increases testing surface for serving runtime (kernel/quantization matrix).
- How to measure subjective quality (conciseness vs correctness)? Need micro-evals and sample prompt sets per vertical.

Dependencies: 
- Serving runtime: support for explicit profile flags in routing engine and automatic model-variant selection.
- Console: UI for profile toggle, cost estimator and sample prompt gallery.
- Billing: ability to apply soft quotas and present upgrade prompts.
- Evals infra: quick micro-eval suite for apprentice profiles.

Notes to self (quick bullets):
- Prototype SDK flag and route tag first; avoid Console work until basic telemetry proves hypothesis.
- Try two model profile candidates: aggressive (mini-quantized + heavy truncation) vs balanced (small-quantized + mild truncation).
- Create 20 seed prompts per vertical (search, assistant, summarization) to run QA micro-evals.

Unresolved: 
- Default per-team quota sizing heuristic (per dev per day? per API key?).
- How to present "quality mode" prompts: explicit hint vs automatic classification?

Action items: 
- [Bianca] build SDK prototype: RedwoodClient(apprentice=True) + header emission (1 week)
- [Arjun] add simple route tag support for apprentice profiles in routing layer (2 weeks)
- [Maya] outline Console quickstart copy and cost slider mock (1 week)
- Sync with infra + billing to confirm quotas and escalation messaging (meeting request)

Links / references: 
- Existing docs: prompt-economics-wizard-notes.json, compact-response-allocator-proto-prd.json (see Drive for related patterns)

Random brainstorm fragments (keep as stash):
- "Apprentice learning checklist": inline hints in Console that suggest prompt edits to reduce tokens.
- "Buddy mode": pair apprentice sessions with example completions to show side-by-side concise vs full fidelity outputs.
- "Progressive fidelity": start answers concise; allow user to request expansion with "more" button which charges additional tokens.

End of sketch. Will iterate after initial prototype telemetry.
